answer: The protocol requires agents to maintain 1,000 unique data shards for identity, verified by unpredictable retrieval audits. An honest agent incurs a baseline disk cost, while 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times that expense to mirror distinct content. Like a structural cedar beam, the verifier probes deep for integrity. The shard acts as a relic of proof, ensuring identity uniqueness across the network. Similar to managing an orchard of distinct trees, any failure to return segments during an audit triggers an immediate, non-refundable slash to funds.
